name: Foreigner's Permanent Residence Permit -- Investor track (Five-Star Card)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires actually-paid-in registered capital of at least USD 2,000,000 in a Chinese enterprise, maintained at or above this level continuously for 3 years.
requirements.fix_path: Structure and maintain a qualifying investment of at least USD 2,000,000 for 3 continuous years.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires actually-paid-in registered capital of at least USD 1,000,000 in a designated central-region province, maintained continuously for 3 years -- half the general-track threshold, a deliberate regional-development incentive.
requirements.fix_path: Structure and maintain a qualifying central-region investment of at least USD 1,000,000 for 3 continuous years.

requirement_groups.name: Investment in western-region provinces or designated poverty-alleviation counties

requirements.blocker_text: Requires actually-paid-in registered capital of at least USD 500,000 in a designated western-region province or a national key poverty-alleviation county, maintained continuously for 4 years -- a longer holding period than the other three tracks, in exchange for the lowest capital floor.
requirements.fix_path: Structure and maintain a qualifying investment of at least USD 500,000 in an eligible western/poverty-alleviation location for 4 continuous years.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires actually-paid-in registered capital of at least USD 500,000 in an industry listed as 'encouraged' under the state Foreign Investment Industry Guidance Catalogue, maintained continuously for 3 years -- the same capital floor as the western/poverty-county track but with the shorter 3-year holding period, rewarding investment in nationally-prioritised sectors over any-industry investment in a low-cost region.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm the target industry is listed as 'encouraged' in the current Guidance Catalogue and structure a qualifying investment of at least USD 500,000 for 3 continuous years.

evidence_required.document: Registered-capital payment records showing the qualifying amount actually paid in (not merely committed)
Health certificate from a Chinese government-designated quarantine authority or an authenticated foreign equivalent

outcome.duration_length: indefinite (card itself valid 10 years for adults, 5 for minors, renewed as a card only)

sources.title: National Immigration Administration (nia.gov.cn) -- 外国人在中国永久居留审批管理办法 (Administrative Measures for the Approval of Foreigners' Permanent Residence in China), Article setting the four investor-track capital tiers

Dongguan Municipal Overseas Chinese Affairs Federation (ql.dg.gov.cn, a local government body) -- official public notice reproducing the four investor-track thresholds verbatim, corroborating the nia.gov.cn regulation independently

notes: SOURCING UPGRADE during this build: an initial draft of this route rested on a single tier-3 immigration-consultancy figure (a USD 500,000-2,000,000 range, described as varying 'by region and sector' without further detail). A direct nia.gov.cn fetch of the actual regulation -- 外国人在中国永久居留审批管理办法 (Administrative Measures for the Approval of Foreigners' Permanent Residence in China) -- resolved this into four distinct, precisely-thresholded OR-logic tracks, independently cross-confirmed by a Dongguan municipal government reproduction of the same figures. This is a clean example of this dataset's core method working as intended: the tier-3 range wasn't wrong, just imprecise, and the direct government fetch replaced an approximation with the actual four-tier structure lawmakers built. The deliberate regional-development gradient is itself a genuine structural finding worth surfacing: central-region investment costs half the general-track threshold (USD 1M vs 2M) for the same 3-year hold, while western-region/poverty-county investment costs only a quarter (USD 500K) but demands a full extra year (4 years vs 3) -- a clear policy design rewarding investment in less-developed regions with a lower capital bar, at the cost of a longer commitment period. Same top-level citizenship/dual-nationality findings apply here as noted in the earlier draft: Green Card status does not itself lead to or accelerate citizenship, which requires an entirely separate naturalisation application (see cn_naturalisation).
